correctness.rationale: Two independently implemented exact functional-graph algorithms exhaust all 3^13 states for each threshold and agree on every entry-period cell and basin multiplicity. Sharp witness populations are nonzero, 78 directly constructed affine wave states equal the entire 13-cycle periodic set, and all methods replay successfully from delivered files. Finite computation is exhaustive for these fixed graph parameters, not a proof about larger graphs.

evidence: Published induced-density criterion: extinction for threshold strictly above maximum induced edge density. The 13-vertex six-regular Paley graph has density exactly three.
Published geometric excitation contraction applies only when the contact threshold exceeds half the maximum degree: here the half degree is three.
Published half-degree rigidity applies to immediately primitive-three configurations, not a complete higher-period census.
Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff (2018) pp. 3324–3328 and Doba (2018) pp. 102–104 define one-contact excitation, unlike thresholds two and three here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strict-density and above-half-degree criteria do not imply extinction at the critical equality threshold three and do not supply periods or exact basin populations at threshold two. The half-degree immediate-three-cycle restriction can rule out that one cycle type at threshold three because 13 is not a multiple of three, but does not eliminate all possible longer periods or bound transient depth. Published one-contact general results study a different map.

evidence: The published density theorem requires ρ(G)<θ; at θ=3, ρ(Paley13)=39/13=3, and at θ=2 the inequality fails even more strongly.
The published contraction theorem requires θ>Δ/2=3, so neither threshold two nor three meets its hypothesis.
Half-degree rigidity constrains initially primitive-three periodic states, whereas the new claim includes all orbit types, all states, 13-period waves, sharp depths, and basin multiplicities.

The threshold-one finite-graph literature cannot imply an exact transition law at thresholds two and three by monotonicity: the complete state map changes and trajectories are not order preserving among the three states.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The nearest general results either have false hypotheses at the claimed parameters or characterize strictly weaker/special periodic behavior. The new finite exact counts, 13-wave affine classification and critical boundary extinction are therefore not demonstrated consequences of those prior theorems.

value.rationale: The natural smallest nontrivial prime-order Paley conference graph exhibits six geometrically classifiable 13-period waves at threshold two, surprisingly long sharp depth fourteen, and critical half-degree universal extinction in four updates after increasing threshold to three. The full exact basin distribution supplies a usable, mathematically motivated benchmark rather than a single arbitrary state count.
